summary: This program asks for a temperature in Celsius, converts it to Fahrenheit, and prints the result. It wraps the work in a try-catch so that typing something that is not a number produces a friendly message instead of a crash.

lines.text: Using print instead of println leaves the cursor on the same line, so the reader types their answer right after the prompt.
This is a try-with-resources statement: the Scanner is created here and Java closes it automatically when the block ends, whether it finishes normally or fails.
The typed line is read as text, trim removes stray spaces, and Double.parseDouble turns it into a number. This is the line that throws NumberFormatException when the text is not numeric.
The conversion itself lives in its own function, so main stays focused on talking to the user.
This catch handles the one problem we can predict exactly, so the reader gets advice about entering a number rather than a generic apology.
A broader safety net for anything else that might go wrong. Order matters: the specific NumberFormatException must be listed before the general Exception, or it would never be reached.
A static helper function, so main can call it without creating an object of this class.
Multiplying by 9 before dividing by 5 keeps the arithmetic in double precision, giving the correct answer for fractional temperatures.
